title: Demand-driven HC Scale & Price-Curve Workbook
content:
Purpose:
A compact workbook used to test simultaneous headcount-scaling policies and price-per-1k-token moves. Focus: short-term (next 6 quarters) impact to cash burn, unit economics, and SLA-backed throughput plans when price changes trigger demand shifts. This is an exploratory sheet (not final) — expected gaps: customer churn modeling, embedded feature segmentation.

Key high-level assumptions:
- Baseline ARR recognition cadence: monthly usage-based revenue ramp = recognized monthly on usage.
- Baseline price per 1k tokens (hosted API): $0.20 (current list)
- Elasticity: measured as % demand change per 10% price change.
  - Conservative: elasticity = -0.05 per 10% (inelastic)
  - Base: elasticity = -0.20 per 10%
  - Aggressive: elasticity = -0.45 per 10% (sensitive consumer workloads)
- Average tokens per request = 1.6k
- Average revenue per request = price_per_1k * 1.6
- Variable infra cost per 1k tokens (GPU+ops) baseline = $0.035
- Contribution margin excludes fixed FC from headcount; headcount drives fixed OPEX and therefore gross margin after absorption.

Headcount plan (quarterly snapshot, hires phasing shown as FTEs added in quarter):
Columns: Role | Q1_FTE | Q2_FTE | Q3_FTE | Q4_FTE | Avg Loaded Cost / FTE / month
SRE | 6 | 8 | 10 | 11 | $18,000
Infra Eng | 8 | 10 | 12 | 13 | $17,500
Applied ML | 5 | 7 | 9 | 10 | $20,000
Product (Console) | 4 | 5 | 5 | 5 | $14,000
Sales (ARR ops + AE) | 10 | 12 | 14 | 15 | $13,000
Customer Success | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | $11,000
Finance & Legal | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | $12,000
Total FTEs | 42 | 52 | 61 | 66 | -

Hiring lags and cash impact notes:
- New hires assumed 60% productivity ramp in first month, 90% by month 3.
- Recruiting pipeline: target time-to-hire = 8 weeks for infra/applied ML, 6 weeks for non-core.
- One-time hiring overhead: $7.5k per hire (relocation/RSU admin/agency fees) applied in quarter of hire.

Scenario slices (apply to each quarter):
1) Price increase +10% from baseline ($0.22/1k) with Base elasticity (-0.20 per 10%). Expected demand change = -20%.
2) Price decrease -15% ($0.17/1k) with Aggressive elasticity (-0.45 per 10%) scaled appropriately => expected demand change = +67.5% (note: clipped at +40% for capacity constraints in simulation unless Dedicated reserved capacity added).
3) No price change but targeted savings via quantization and batching reduce variable infra cost by 18% (new var cost = $0.0287/1k).

Model outputs (quarterly, simplified columns):
Columns: Scenario | Price/1k | Demand delta (%) | Monthly throughput (b tokens) | Revenue change (%) | Variable cost change (%) | Net contribution delta ($k)
Baseline | $0.20 | 0% | 6.0 | 0% | 0% | 0
Price +10% (Base) | $0.22 | -20% | 4.8 | -4.0% | 0% | -$350k (estimate)
Price -15% (Aggressive) | $0.17 | +40% (capped) | 8.4 | +30% | +40% | +$420k (estimate)
Batch/quantopt | $0.20 | 0% | 6.0 | 0% | -18% | +$180k (estimate)

Interpretation notes:
- Small price increases can reduce revenue in near-term when demand elasticity is above ~0.15 per 10% because throughput drop compounds pricing effect; see "Price +10%" line.
- Aggressive price cuts can boost top-line but may require immediate burst capacity; without Dedicated commit we model capped demand at +40% due to capacity/latency SLO constraints — this is a conservative operational guardrail.
- Cost-savings from quantization/batching are high ROI and show up as positive contribution without needing demand expansion. Prioritize Optimize pipeline.

Cash burn and runway sensitivity (6-quarter view):
- If we enact Price -15% and hire to support +40% demand, incremental monthly cash burn increases from hiring until revenue ramps (~3 quarters). Net effect over 6 quarters is neutral-to-positive if CAC stays below 15% of incremental revenue.
- If we enact Price +10% and hold hiring plan, burn increases due to lost revenue while fixed costs remain.

Action items & open questions (for finance + growth):
- (Priya) Run customer cohort-level elasticity tests for top 50 accounts (JIRA FIN-9872) to validate aggregate elasticity assumption.
- (Sofia) Simulate capacity plan for Dedicated commit options if demand > +25% — include cost trade vs burst on cloud marketplaces.
- (Tom) Re-run model replacing capped demand with a soft-latency penalty curve to estimate churn vs degraded SLOs.
- Validate per-FTE loaded cost with People Ops (confirm bonus/RSU accrual treatment).

Sheet tabs outline (what to expect if we convert to a multi-tab sheet):
- assumptions (single-page)
- hires_by_month (detailed monthly hires, ramp curves, one-time costs)
- price_sensitivity_grid (matrix of price moves vs elasticity pairs)
- capacity_impact (latency SLO overlay, Dedicated commit modeling)
- cash_runway (6-quarter P&L with scenarios)

Reviewer notes (quick):
- This is intentionally compact to support an early cross-functional meeting. Numbers are rounded; treat all dollar deltas as directional.
- Avoid presenting externally without sign-off from Finance head and Growth.

Version log:
- 2026-11-04: initial draft (Ethan)
- 2026-11-09: added capped demand rule and hiring lags (Priya)
- 2026-11-12: updated per-FTE loaded costs and initial scenario run (Sofia)
